newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss National Bank rules out gold sales for now.
newsitem.headline: Swiss National Bank rules out gold sales for now.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank cannot sell any of its gold reserves until the country's constitution is amended in a reform process that could take years, SNB Chairman Hans Meyer told a Swiss newspaper.

The central bank wants to make its investment policy more flexible to boost its return on official currency reserves, and the legal framework for this could be in place later this year, he told the SonntagsZeitung in an interview published Sunday.
But the idea of selling gold, as the Dutch central bank has recently acknowledged doing, is complicated by the constitutional mandate for the SNB to back its banknotes with gold, he added.
"Our gold reserves as well are the property of the people, but one must weigh very carefully which aims one should use in drawing on National Bank assets," Meyer said.
"At the moment, however, we have no freedom to act at all. This requires a constitutional amendment. In the best case, the constitutional project will come up for a vote at the end of 1998," he said.

Speculation about central bank gold sales has weighed on gold prices for months. Traders fear some European Union banks could sell gold to boost national income and qualify this year as founding members of Europe's single currency in 1999.
